articles.dek: Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked…
articles.description: Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1. Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. articles.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
articles.dek: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade.…
articles.description: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation. Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager. Continue reading...

articles.description: If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park. Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team and he certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside, where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back commendably to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance. At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and subtle tactical rejig suggested he is no mug after all. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.
